The mean, median, mode and range of your numbers are all equal to each other but they are not equal to {@aa@}!

Worked solution:

There are many ways to approach this question and the solutions are not unique. Here is one method to answer the question (can you think of any others?):

We start with the median. Let the median \(=\) {@third_num@}.

\( \_,\_,{@third_num@},\_,\_.\)

We know that {@third_num@} is also the mode, so there will have to be a {@sec_num@} before or after. Let us choose before.

\( \_,{@third_num@},{@third_num@},\_,\_.\)

We know that the first and last numbers need to be {@aa@} apart and that the sum of the numbers has to be \(5 \times {@aa@} = {@ev(5*aa)@}\) because the mean is {@aa@}. Try:

\( {@first_num-1@},{@third_num@},{@third_num@},\_,{@fifth_num-1@}.\)

These add up to {@first_num-1@}+{@third_num@}+{@third_num@}+{@fifth_num-1@} ={@ev(first_num-1+third_num+third_num+fifth_num-1)@}, so the missing number would have to be {@ev(5*aa)@} - {@ev(first_num-1+third_num+third_num+fifth_num-1)@} = {@ev((5*aa)-(first_num-1+third_num+third_num+fifth_num-1))@}. But this will mess up our range as it is bigger than {@fifth_num-1@} which is meant to be our largest number! So it cannot be {@first_num-1@} and {@fifth_num-1@}. We need bigger numbers. Try:

\( {@first_num@},{@third_num@},{@third_num@},\_,{@fifth_num@}.\)

These add up to {@first_num@}+{@third_num@}+{@third_num@}+{@fifth_num@} ={@ev(first_num+third_num+third_num+fifth_num)@}, so the missing number would have to be {@ev(5*aa)@} - {@ev(first_num+third_num+third_num+fifth_num)@} = {@ev((5*aa)-(first_num+third_num+third_num+fifth_num))@}.

So the five numbers are {@ta_list@}.

There is more than one solution.
